claims.text: The initial equiatomic FeCoNiPd alloy is single-phase FCC.
The initial FeCoNiPd alloy is prepared by arc melting and homogenization at 1000 °C for 24 h in vacuum.
Adding Al so that it constitutes 20 at.% produces equiatomic FeCoNiPdAl.
The specified Al addition and thermal treatment will form B2-type precipitates in FeCoNiPdAl.
The B2-type precipitates will be enriched in Al and Pd.
The Al–Pd-rich precipitates will be coherent with the FCC matrix.
The precipitates will have characteristic sizes of 20–50 nm.
Coherent precipitate/matrix interfaces will pin magnetic domain walls.
The precipitate interfaces will increase magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Domain-wall pinning will impede magnetization reversal and raise coercivity.
Equiatomic FeCoNiPd processed under the baseline treatment has a room-temperature coercivity of approximately 20 Oe.
Aged FeCoNiPdAl will have a room-temperature coercivity above 100 Oe.
Aged FeCoNiPdAl will have at least five times the coercivity of the FeCoNiPd baseline.
The prediction applies to equiatomic FeCoNiPdAl arc-melted under Ar, homogenized at 1000 °C for 24 h, aged at 500 °C for 24 h under vacuum, and furnace-cooled.
Other compositions or thermal treatments may fail to form the required B2 precipitates.
The kinetics and thermodynamics of Al–Pd ordering in FeCoNiPdAl are not established and may require optimization of aging parameters.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a fivefold coercivity increase, but the hypothesis is falsified only when the increase is less than twofold. An outcome between twofold and fivefold would fail the stated prediction without meeting the stated falsification criterion.
